meanings.usage: 指根据现有信息推断未来事件
指提前知道或预见将要发生的事

meanings.meaning: 声名狼藉地（修饰形容词，强调某事出名（通常指坏的方面））

meanings.usage: 指大型计算机系统，通常用于企业或政府机构
形容早期、技术不发达的事物
指容易使用和理解的产品或系统
指结合文字、图像、声音等多种媒介的技术
指拒绝接受或不认真考虑某个想法
与of连用，表示具备做某事的能力
主要用于医学领域，指判断疾病
指不再稀奇、变得普通的事物
表示即时发生，没有延迟
形容值得注意或不同寻常的事物
常与of连用，表示免除某人的负担或工作
指涉及电子技术的设备或系统

phrases.usage: 早在...（用于强调时间久远）

examples.en: As long ago as the 1960s, Leon Bagrit predicted these uses.
examples.zh: 早在20世纪60年代，莱昂·巴格瑞特就预测到了这些用途。

examples.en: It pointed the way to the future.
Many of their functions have been taken over by small personal computers.
examples.zh: 许多功能已被小型个人电脑所取代。

examples.en: They would be capable of providing information about traffic jams.
examples.zh: 它们将能够提供有关交通拥堵的信息。

phrases.usage: 解除某人的...；使某人从...中解脱

examples.en: They would relieve office workers of dull, repetitive clerical work.
examples.zh: 它们将把办公室工作人员从枯燥重复的文书工作中解放出来。

phrases.usage: 他也无法预见（用于否定句后加强语气）

examples.en: Nor could he have foreseen the development of the Internet.
examples.zh: 他也不可能预见互联网的发展。
与电话网络相连的计算机。

examples.en: Computers have become more and more powerful.
examples.zh: 计算机变得越来越强大。

phrases.phrase: it is even more remarkable that

examples.en: It is even more remarkable that an Englishman could predict these uses.
examples.zh: 更值得注意的是一个英国人能够预测这些用途。

examples.en: Bagrit dismissed the idea that computers would learn to 'think' for themselves.
examples.zh: 巴格瑞特摒弃了计算机会学会'独立思考'的观念。

grammar.title: 情态动词 + have + 过去分词（表达对过去的推测或可能性）
grammar.definition: 情态动词could/might/must + have + 过去分词结构用于表达对过去事件的推测、批评或惊讶 这个结构用于：1) 对过去的推测（could have been, might have been）；2) 虚拟语气中的假设；3) 表达'本可以'但未实现的可能性

examples.en: Who could have imagined, in the mid 1970s, that computers would be common in homes?
examples.zh: 在20世纪70年代中期，有谁能够想象计算机会在家庭中普及？

examples.en: Leon Bagrit couldn't possibly have foreseen the development of the Internet.
examples.zh: 莱昂·巴格瑞特不可能预见互联网的发展。

examples.en: If he were alive today, he might be able to tell us what to expect.
examples.zh: 如果他今天还活着，他也许能告诉我们该期待什么。

grammar.title: nor/neither...nor 的倒装用法
grammar.structure: Nor/Neither + 助动词/be动词/情态动词 + 主语 + ... .
grammar.definition: 当nor或neither...nor连接两个否定成分时，可以使用倒装语序 用于否定句后，连接第二个否定成分，强调两者都不。nor could he have foreseen是'他也无法预见'的意思，强调连...也无法做到

examples.en: Nor could he have foreseen the development of the Internet.
examples.zh: 他也不可能预见互联网的发展。

examples.en: Neither does he want to go, nor will he change his mind.
examples.zh: 他既不想去，也不会改变主意。

grammar.title: 过去完成时在间接引语中的使用
grammar.structure: 主句动词（过去时）+ that + 主语 + had + 过去分词
grammar.definition: 当主句动词是过去时，间接引语中的动词通常需要使用过去完成时 用于报道过去某人所说的话或想法，使时间关系更加清晰。Bagrit foresaw a time when computers would be small...中，would表示过去的将来

examples.en: Bagrit dismissed the idea that computers would learn to 'think' for themselves.
examples.zh: 巴格瑞特摒弃了计算机会学会'独立思考'的观念。

examples.en: He predicted that computers would be small enough to hold in the hand.
examples.zh: 他预测计算机会小到可以握在手中。

original.en: Who could have imagined, in the mid 1970s, that by the end of the 20th century, computers would be as common in people's homes as TV sets?
original.zh: 在20世纪70年代中期，有谁能够想象到20世纪末计算机会像电视机一样普及到家庭中？

imitations.en: Who could have imagined, in the 1990s, that smartphones would replace cameras?
imitations.zh: 在90年代，有谁能够想象智能手机会取代相机？

imitations.en: Who could have predicted that AI would develop so rapidly?
imitations.zh: 有谁能够预测人工智能会发展得如此迅速？

original.en: Of course, Leon Bagrit couldn't possibly have foreseen the development of the Internet.
original.zh: 当然，莱昂·巴格瑞特不可能预见互联网的发展。

imitations.en: The ancient Egyptians couldn't possibly have foreseen modern technology.
imitations.zh: 古埃及人不可能预见现代科技。

imitations.en: Early scientists couldn't possibly have imagined the internet.
imitations.zh: 早期的科学家不可能想象到互联网。

patterns.pattern: It is even more remarkable that...

original.en: Considering how recent these developments are, it is even more remarkable that as long ago as the 1960s, an Englishman was able to predict some of these uses.
original.zh: 考虑到这些发展是多么新近，尤其值得注意的是，早在20世纪60年代，一个英国人就能预测到其中一些用途。

imitations.en: It is even more remarkable that he solved the problem in minutes.
imitations.zh: 更值得注意的是他在几分钟内就解决了这个问题。

imitations.en: It is even more remarkable that she learned three languages in a year.
imitations.zh: 更值得注意的是她在一年内学会了三种语言。

patterns.pattern: ...when they would be capable of doing...

original.en: Bagrit foresaw a time when computers would be small enough to hold in the hand, when they would be capable of providing information about traffic jams.
original.zh: 巴格瑞特预见了这样一个时代：计算机会小到可以握在手中，能够提供交通拥堵信息。

imitations.en: Scientists foresee a time when robots would be capable of doing all housework.
imitations.zh: 科学家预见了机器人能够做所有家务的时代。

imitations.en: He imagined a future when people would be capable of traveling to Mars.
imitations.zh: 他想象人们能够前往火星的未来。

lines.en: is notoriously difficult.
lines.zh: 众所周知，预测未来是非常困难的。

lines.en: Who could have imagined, in the mid 1970s, for example, that by the end of the 20th century, computers would be as common in people's homes as TV sets?
lines.zh: 举个例子吧，在20世纪70年代中叶又有谁能想得到在20世纪末的时候，家庭用的计算机会像电视机一样普遍？

lines.en: In the 1970s, computers were common enough, but only in big business, government departments, and large organizations.
lines.zh: 在70年代，计算机已经相当普及了，但只用在大公司，政府部门和大的组织之中，它们被称为主机。

lines.en: These were the so-called mainframe machines.
lines.zh: 计算机主机确实很大，常常占据了装有空调的多间房间，雇用专职的技师，而且得用专门编写的软件才能运行。

lines.en: Mainframe computers were very large indeed, often occupying whole air-conditioned rooms, employing full-time technicians and run on specially-written software.
lines.zh: 虽然这种大计算机仍然存在，但它们的许多功能已被体积小但功能齐全的个人电脑——即我们常说的PC机——所代替了。

lines.en: Though these large machines still exist, many of their functions have been taken over by small powerful personal computers, commonly known as PCs.
lines.zh: 1975年，美国推出了一台被称为“牛郎星”的原始机型。

lines.en: In 1975, a primitive machine called the Altair, was launched in the USA.
lines.zh: 严格地说起来，它可以被称为第一台“家用电脑”，而且它也指了今后的方向。

lines.en: It can properly be described as the first 'home computer' and it pointed the way to the future.
lines.zh: 70年代末，在牛郎星之后又出现了一种被称为“苹果”的机型。

lines.en: This was followed, at the end of the 1970s, by a machine called an Apple.
lines.zh: 80年代初，计算机行业的王牌公司美国国际商用机器公司（IBM）生产出了世界上第一台个人电脑。

lines.en: In the early 1980s, the computer giant, IBM produced the world's first Personal Computer.
lines.zh: 这种电脑采用了一种被称为磁盘操作系统（DOS）的工作程序，而这种程序是由当时规模不大的微软公司生产的。

lines.en: This ran on an 'operating system' called DOS, produced by a then small company named Microsoft.
lines.zh: IBM的个人电脑被大规模地模仿。

lines.en: The IBM Personal Computer was widely copied.
lines.zh: 从那些简陋的初级阶段，我们看到了现在都已普及的、使用简便的家用电脑和多媒体的微机的发展。

lines.en: From those humble beginnings, we have seen the development of the user-friendly home computers and multimedia machines which are in common use today.
lines.zh: 想一想这些发展的时间多么短，就更觉得英国人莱昂。

lines.en: Considering how recent these developments are, it is even more remarkable that as long ago as the 1960s, an Englishman, Leon Bagrit, was able to predict some of the uses of computers which we know today.
lines.zh: 巴格瑞特有着非凡的能力。

lines.en: Bagrit dismissed the idea that computers would learn to 'think' for themselves and would 'rule the world', which people liked to believe in those days.
lines.zh: 他在60年代就能预言我们今天知道的计算机的一些用途。

lines.en: Bagrit foresaw a time when computers would be small enough to hold in the hand, when they would be capable of providing information about traffic jams and suggesting alternative routes, when they would be used in hospitals to help doctors to diagnose illnesses, when they would relieve office workers and accountants of dull, repetitive clerical work.
lines.zh: 巴格瑞特根本不接受计算机可以学会自己去“思考”和计算可以“统治世界”这种想法，而这种想法是当时的人们都愿意相信的。巴格瑞特预示有一天计算机可以小到拿在手上，计算机可以使办公室人员和会计免除那些枯燥、重复的劳动。

lines.en: All these computer uses have become commonplace .
lines.zh: 计算机的所有这些功能现在都变得很平常。

lines.en: Of course, Leon Bagrit could not possibly have foreseen the development of the Internet, the worldwide system that enables us to communicate instantly with anyone in any part of the world by using computers linked to telephone networks.
lines.zh: 当然了，莱昂。巴格瑞特根本没有可能预测到国际交互网——就是把计算机连结到电话线路上，以便和世界上任何一个地方的人立即进行联系的一个世界范围的通讯系统——的发展。

lines.en: Nor could he have foreseen how we could use the Internet to obtain information on every known subject, so we can read it on a screen in our homes and even print it as well if we want to.
lines.zh: 他也无法预测到我们可以利用国际交互网获取有关任何已知专题的信息，以便在家里的屏幕上阅读，如果愿意的话甚至可以将其打印出来。

lines.en: Computers have become smaller and smaller, more and more powerful and cheaper and cheaper.
lines.zh: 计算机已经变得体积越来越小，功能越来越多，价格越来越低，这就是莱昂。

lines.en: This is what makes Leon Bagrit's predictions particularly remarkable.
lines.zh: 巴格瑞特的预测非凡的地方。

lines.en: If he, or someone like him, were alive today, he might be able to tell us what to expect in the next fifty years.
lines.zh: 如果他或是像他的什么人今天还活着的话，他大概可以告诉我们下一个50年后会发生什么事情。

questions.q: What was the 'future' electronic development that Leon Bagrit wasn't able to foresee?
questions.zh: 莱昂·巴格瑞特未能预见到的'未来'电子发展是什么？
questions.a: The development of the Internet, the worldwide system that links computers to telephone networks and lets us communicate instantly with anyone anywhere.
questions.aZh: 国际互联网的发展——把计算机连接到电话网络、可与世界任何地方的人即时通讯的世界性系统。
questions.hint: 见课文 'could not possibly have foreseen the development of the Internet...'

questions.q: In the 1970s, where were computers mainly used?
questions.zh: 20世纪70年代，计算机主要用在什么地方？
questions.a: Only in big business, government departments and large organizations — the so-called mainframe machines.
questions.aZh: 只用在大公司、政府部门和大的组织之中，即所谓的主机。
questions.hint: 见 'but only in big business, government departments, and large organizations'

questions.q: What was the Altair, launched in the USA in 1975?
questions.zh: 1975年在美国推出的'牛郎星'是什么？
questions.a: A primitive machine that can properly be described as the first 'home computer' and that pointed the way to the future.
questions.aZh: 一台原始机型，严格来说可称为第一台'家用电脑'，并指明了未来的方向。
questions.hint: 见 'In 1975, a primitive machine called the Altair...' 及下一句

questions.q: What idea did Bagrit dismiss, and what did he foresee instead?
questions.zh: 巴格瑞特不接受什么想法，又预示了什么？
questions.a: He dismissed the idea that computers would learn to 'think' and 'rule the world'; he foresaw small hand-held computers that give traffic information, help doctors diagnose illnesses and relieve clerks of dull work.
questions.aZh: 他不接受计算机会学会自己'思考'并'统治世界'的想法；他预示计算机可小到拿在手上、提供路况信息、辅助医生诊断、免除职员的枯燥工作。
questions.hint: 见 'Bagrit dismissed the idea...' 与 'Bagrit foresaw a time when...'

questions.q: Why does the author think Leon Bagrit's predictions are particularly remarkable?
questions.zh: 作者为什么认为莱昂·巴格瑞特的预测格外非凡？
questions.a: Because in the 1960s, long before personal computers existed, he already predicted many computer uses we take for granted today; given how recent these developments are, such foresight looks all the more remarkable.
questions.aZh: 因为在个人电脑尚未出现的20世纪60年代，他就已预见了我们今天习以为常的许多计算机用途；考虑到这些发展距今如此之近，这样的先见之明就更显得非凡。
questions.hint: 见 'Considering how recent these developments are, it is even more remarkable...' 及文末 'This is what makes...'

translation:
众所周知，预测未来是非常困难的。
举个例子吧，在20世纪70年代中叶又有谁能想得到在20世纪末的时候，家庭用的计算机会像电视机一样普遍？
在70年代，计算机已经相当普及了，但只用在大公司，政府部门和大的组织之中，它们被称为主机。
计算机主机确实很大，常常占据了装有空调的多间房间，雇用专职的技师，而且得用专门编写的软件才能运行。
虽然这种大计算机仍然存在，但它们的许多功能已被体积小但功能齐全的个人电脑——即我们常说的PC机——所代替了。
1975年，美国推出了一台被称为“牛郎星”的原始机型。
严格地说起来，它可以被称为第一台“家用电脑”，而且它也指了今后的方向。
70年代末，在牛郎星之后又出现了一种被称为“苹果”的机型。
80年代初，计算机行业的王牌公司美国国际商用机器公司（IBM）生产出了世界上第一台个人电脑。
这种电脑采用了一种被称为磁盘操作系统（DOS）的工作程序，而这种程序是由当时规模不大的微软公司生产的。
IBM的个人电脑被大规模地模仿。
从那些简陋的初级阶段，我们看到了现在都已普及的、使用简便的家用电脑和多媒体的微机的发展。
想一想这些发展的时间多么短，就更觉得英国人莱昂。
巴格瑞特有着非凡的能力。
他在60年代就能预言我们今天知道的计算机的一些用途。
巴格瑞特根本不接受计算机可以学会自己去“思考”和计算可以“统治世界”这种想法，而这种想法是当时的人们都愿意相信的。
巴格瑞特预示有一天计算机可以小到拿在手上，计算机可以使办公室人员和会计免除那些枯燥、重复的劳动。
计算机的所有这些功能现在都变得很平常。
当然了，莱昂。
巴格瑞特根本没有可能预测到国际交互网——就是把计算机连结到电话线路上，以便和世界上任何一个地方的人立即进行联系的一个世界范围的通讯系统——的发展。
他也无法预测到我们可以利用国际交互网获取有关任何已知专题的信息，以便在家里的屏幕上阅读，如果愿意的话甚至可以将其打印出来。
计算机已经变得体积越来越小，功能越来越多，价格越来越低，这就是莱昂。
巴格瑞特的预测非凡的地方。
如果他或是像他的什么人今天还活着的话，他大概可以告诉我们下一个50年后会发生什么事情。
title: Predicting the Future
subtitle: 预测未来

lead.question: 为什么说莱昂·巴格瑞特在20世纪60年代对计算机未来的预测格外非凡？
lead.warmup: 本课回顾计算机从笨重主机到个人电脑、再到国际互联网的惊人演变，并介绍英国人莱昂·巴格瑞特。他在20世纪60年代就预言了今天电脑的许多用途，却没能预见互联网的诞生。边读边想：预测未来为何如此困难？注意体会 predict、foresee 与将来时、虚拟语气的表达。
goals: 掌握 predict、foresee、forecast 等表示'预测'的动词用法。
理解并运用 would 与过去将来时描述从过去看将来的事。
辨析 though 引导的让步从句和 Nor 置句首的倒装结构。
体会与现在事实相反的虚拟语气（If he were alive today...）。
lead.summary: 课文以计算机的演变为线索：从占据整间空调房的主机，到1975年的牛郎星、苹果机与IBM个人电脑，再到今天小巧廉价的电脑和多媒体设备。作者由此赞叹莱昂·巴格瑞特：在个人电脑尚未问世的60年代，他就预言了掌上电脑、路况提示、辅助诊断等用途，却没能预见互联网。
lead.tips: predict 强调凭知识'预言、预测'未来，forecast 多指依据数据的'预报'（天气、经济）；foresee 意为'预见到'，后接名词或从句，别与 look forward to（期待）混淆。

exercises.q: 汉译英：众所周知，预测未来是非常困难的。
exercises.a: It is notoriously difficult to predict the future.

exercises.q: 填空：Who could have ____ (imagine), in the mid 1970s, that computers ____ (be) as common in people's homes as TV sets?
exercises.note: could have done 表过去推测

exercises.q: 句型转换：These large machines still exist. Many of their functions have been taken over by small powerful personal computers.（用 Though 合并为一句）
exercises.a: Though these large machines still exist, many of their functions have been taken over by small powerful personal computers.

exercises.q: 填空（虚拟语气）：If he, or someone like him, ____ (be) alive today, he ____ (be) able to tell us what to expect in the next fifty years.
exercises.note: 与现在相反的虚拟语气

exercises.q: 改错：Nor he could have foreseen how we could use the Internet to obtain information.
exercises.a: Nor could he have foreseen how we could use the Internet to obtain information.

exercises.q: 汉译英：巴格瑞特预示有一天计算机可以小到拿在手上。
exercises.a: Bagrit foresaw a time when computers would be small enough to hold in the hand.
exercises.note: a time when 引导定语从句

exercises.q: 汉译英：天气预报说明天将有大雨。
exercises.a: The weather forecast says there will be heavy rain tomorrow.
exercises.note: forecast 多指天气/经济预报

quiz.q: 课文认为，20世纪70年代的计算机主要使用在哪些地方？
options: In big business, government departments and large organizations.
quiz.note: 文中说明当时只在机关、企业和大型组织使用。

quiz.q: 1975年在美国推出、被称为第一台'家用电脑'的原始机型是？
quiz.note: Altair 于1975年问世，被视为首台'家用电脑'。

quiz.q: 巴格瑞特拒绝接受 (dismissed) 的关于计算机的想法是什么？
options: That computers would learn to 'think' for themselves and 'rule the world'.
That computers would become smaller and cheaper.
That computers could help doctors diagnose illnesses.
That computers could give advice about traffic jams.
quiz.note: 他否定'计算机会思考并统治世界'之说。

quiz.q: 巴格瑞特没能预见的'未来'电子发展是什么？
options: The use of computers in hospitals.
quiz.note: 他无法预见互联网这一世界性通讯系统。

quiz.q: 课文里 'it pointed the way to the future' 中的 it 指什么？
options: The Altair, the first primitive home computer.
quiz.note: it 承接上句，指代牛郎星机。

quiz.q: 课文最后一句 'If he... were alive today, he might be able to tell us...' 使用了什么语气？
options: The imperative mood, giving an order.
The subjunctive mood, expressing an unreal condition.
The simple present tense, stating a general fact.
The future perfect tense, predicting a result.
quiz.note: were + might be 表达与现在相反的假设。
